title: Google Chrome: use after free in XML, exploited (CVE-2026-125350)
summary: Google updated Chrome's stable channel on 9 November 2026 to 157.0.8103.50/.51 for Windows and Mac and 157.0.8103.50 for Linux. The update fixes CVE-2026-125350, a use after free in XML, which the CVE record (published 10 November) says allowed a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page, in Chrome before 157.0.8103.50. Google's post says: "Google is aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild." CISA had not listed it in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog by its catalog of 9 November. Wardlatch reads the version of the Chrome that is installed (the app's Info.plist on a Mac, dpkg's record on Debian and Ubuntu); it never starts Chrome.

files.label: Mac app
files.reviewWhenFixed: this Chrome, as installed, has the fix; if Chrome was open when it updated, it runs the old version until it restarts (Chrome's menu shows Relaunch), and Wardlatch can't see which version is running

files.reviewWhenFixed: this Chrome, as installed, has the fix; a Chrome that was open when it updated runs the old version until it restarts, and Wardlatch can't see which version is running

versionFiles.fix: Update Chrome to 157.0.8103.50 or later (on a Mac 157.0.8103.50 or .51): open Chrome, go to Settings, About Chrome, let it update, then press Relaunch. On Debian or Ubuntu: sudo apt update && sudo apt install --only-upgrade google-chrome-stable, then restart Chrome.
versionFiles.lookedIn: Chrome's Info.plist in /Applications and ~/Applications, and dpkg's record of google-chrome-stable

reviewFix: Restart Chrome (Chrome's menu shows Relaunch when an update is waiting), so the version that runs is the one installed.
safeText: no Google Chrome found in the places this check reads
notCovered: Other browsers built on Chromium (Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi, Arc), which number their releases their own way and ship the fix on their own schedule; Chromium itself; Chrome's beta, dev and canary channels; Chrome installed by snap, Flatpak or an RPM; ChromeOS, Android and iOS; Electron apps; Windows. Check each one's own release notes.
